evidenceBoundary: Operation 0x30 handler 0x0c11f026 writes operand one to actor +0xf0 and the exact operation pointer to actor +0xec, requests controller mode 7 through 0x0c10d77c, and uses 0x0c11efd2 for zero-ID teardown. The request initializer 0x0c10d7f6 passes the nonzero operand to FUN_0c092f14, whose exclusive registered ranges select the original M_FREE or M_MOBJ sequence. The action ID is therefore a registered motion request, not an opaque action namespace. The actor +0x18d flag marks these as queued requests; actor +0x6c may legitimately be null, and null is never treated as RAM offset zero. A resident controller snapshot remains contextual validation; the static lookup path supplies the action-ID-to-motion mapping. Runtime joins require the resident source-normalized PRG1 hash, its unique owner actor record, the exact action ID, and an operation pointer resolving to that exact source operation. Action IDs remain numeric until independently mapped to authored motion assets.
